result.title: Routeability Before Routing: Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench for Audited LLM Model Selection
result.summary: LLM routing aims to choose, for each prompt, which model in a portfolio is most likely to answer correctly. This only makes sense when the benchmark contains enough prompt-specific variation for different models to be best on different inputs. On coarse-scored LLM benchmarks, however, many models often tie for the best score, and the single best model may already leave little room for improvement. We therefore propose a routeability-first audit, instantiated as RAP and RouteabilityBench, a runnable claim-verification package. The audit is retrospective: it runs once the benchmark-portfolio score matrix exists and before router comparisons are interpreted as general evidence, rather than certifying a portfolio that has not yet been evaluated. Across four benchmarks and 66 LLMs, generic routing enhancements such as larger embedding sets, dimensionality reduction, selective abstention, clustering, and stronger regressors do not consistently outperform the single best model. The clearest positive evidence is concentrated in portfolio-dependent Omni-MATH settings, while GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and IFEval show different ways in which routing can remain hard or predictor-sensitive. Our practical recommendation is that routing gains should be reported together with routeability diagnostics, tied-best analysis, portfolio construction details, and family-corrected statistical tests.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 routeability-first 审计协议 RAP 与 RouteabilityBench，在已有「基准×模型」分数矩阵上检查路由是否具备提升空间，并在 4 个基准、66 个 LLM 上发现常见路由增强通常难以稳定超过单一最佳模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先审计基准的收益空间、并列最优与统计校正」流程可供核查：能否用于辨别 LVR 相对直接回答的增益是否只是被基准饱和或并列评分掩盖，而非真实的状态或证据使用差异。
